title: Anukili
premise: Fiction based on the Igbo myth of Anukili Ugama, set in a mythic past. One story told across an animated series, a game, and shorts.
logline: A boy is born in Aguleri legs first, with teeth, clutching roots and herbs. He grows into the hero who kills the hippopotamus at the stream, turns on his own people in Eziagulu, and dies with burning fire on his head.

characters.name: Anukili Ugama
characters.canon: Huge and tall, with tough, coarse skin, a stomach like a big water pot, a scarred face, bloodshot eyes, lips as thick as tree bark and teeth like elephant tusks. He carries a tree stump, a bow and arrows, and a big stick with thorns at the head.

characters.name: Anukili's father
characters.canon: Rejects him at birth. He calls the birth an abomination, and in his rage decides to kill the baby on the fourth day.

characters.name: The people of Eziagulu
characters.canon: His own people, in Aguleri. The women carry water home in pots. They vow to kill him.

locations.name: Aguleri
locations.description: A village in the time before anyone wrote anything down.

locations.name: Eziagulu
locations.description: His own people live here, in Aguleri. The women carry water home in pots.

locations.name: The stream
locations.description: Water comes from the local stream. A hippopotamus starts attacking people here.

locations.name: The Omabala River
locations.description: Runs across the village. One night they run across the Omabala to escape him.

channels.name: Series
channels.title: Five episodes
channels.pitch: His whole life, from omen to fire, across five episodes.

channels.name: Game
channels.title: The hunt at the stream
channels.pitch: Face the hippopotamus at the stream and learn what the water hides.

channels.name: Shorts
channels.title: The women of Eziagulu
channels.pitch: The women of Eziagulu tell what they saw, each in her own words.

parts.title: The Omen
parts.summary: A boy is born in Aguleri legs first, with upper and lower teeth, clutching roots and herbs in both hands. His father calls it an abomination.
parts.excerpt: He cannot cry until he is seven years old, and then only three times a day: at midnight, in the morning and in the evening. When he cries, animals take to their heels.

parts.title: The Weight
parts.summary: Anukili becomes a leader with no training at all. He eats the food meant for thirty men, and anything he touches comes crashing to the ground.
parts.excerpt: Enyinyi, his confidant and medicine man, stays at his side.

parts.title: The Stream
parts.summary: A hippopotamus starts attacking people at the stream. Anukili asks if they're sure it's a hippopotamus, and calls it tiny.
parts.excerpt: He tells them to show him where it waits, then he kills it.

parts.title: The Pots
parts.summary: At thirty, Anukili turns on his own people in Eziagulu. No quantity of water satisfies him, so he snatches the women's water pots and breaks them with one finger.
parts.excerpt: One night they run across the Omabala to escape him. He finds them, and they run back across the river to endure him again.

parts.title: The Fire
parts.summary: Owl's droppings blind Anukili, and Enyinyi's herbs restore his sight. But the people of Eziagulu have vowed to kill him. Their first plan fails. Their next puts burning fire on his head.
parts.excerpt: The people are in ecstasy. They can't believe their eyes. So Anukili could die after all?
